course_title: Strategic Management of Tourism and Events
course_description:
This capstone course draws together concepts and processes explored within the Tourism and Event Management major and affords an opportunity for the student to apply these concepts in real-world strategic scenarios. It provides conceptual and practical understanding of strategic management and strategic leadership as they apply in the tourism and events industries.

The course covers key areas that are essential for the effective management of tourism and events, including the strategic contexts and outcomes of tourism and events, strategic planning for tourism and events, and implementing tourism and events strategies. Using scenario planning, students will also be invited to become future-focused and lifelong learners. Finally, students will reflect upon the challenges and opportunities that confront managers and leaders, and consider how decisions and solutions can be reached in the context of legal, ethical and professional guidelines.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

TRVT3004 has been revised for Semester 2, 2026 to provide a more scaffolded, applied and engaging learning experience. Assessment 1 now consists of weekly in-class strategic analysis activities, allowing students to progressively develop evidence-based analysis, data interpretation, strategic thinking and communication skills. Assessment 2 has been revised from an individual scenario planning report to a group scenario planning presentation with an individual Q&A component, strengthening collaboration while also verifying each student’s individual understanding. Assessment 3 has been staged into an early leadership aspirations task and a final reflection to encourage deeper and more continuous leadership development.

Tutorials will include more structured group work, data insight activities, authentic Brisbane 2032 scenarios, and clearer weekly templates to help students connect class activities directly to assessment expectations.

course_aims: This course aims to provide students with an in-depth insight into the strategic management of tourism and events, through developing the skills to evaluate strategies at the destination level as well as at the level of individual tourism and events organisations. The course also aims to help students to develop a future focus, both through scenario planning for tourism and events and through a reflective approach to developing their own leadership skills.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply key concepts and processes from the strategic management field to tourism and events organisations.
Collaboratively evaluate strategies both at the micro (organisation) level and the macro (destination) level.
Undertake scenario planning in the tourism and events context to develop a future focus.
Apply an understanding of leadership theories, business practices and related ethics in appraising real world issues and events.
Reflect on your own skills and abilities as a future leader in the tourism and events industry.

assessment_details.task_description: Strategic managers in tourism and events are increasingly required to make decisions in complex, uncertain and rapidly changing environments. Effective strategic decision-making requires the ability to interpret evidence, analyse trends, evaluate competing stakeholder interests, anticipate future challenges, and develop appropriate responses. This assessment is designed to progressively develop these capabilities through a series of structured tutorial activities focused on Brisbane 2032 and the future of tourism and events. This assessment consists of a sequence of seven (7) scaffolded in-class strategic analysis activities completed during Weeks 3–9 tutorials. Students are required to complete a minimum of five (5) activities. Students may choose which activities to complete. Alternatively, students who complete more than five activities (each activity is worth 6%) will have their highest five marks counted towards the final Assessment 1 grade (30%). assessment_details.due_date: Week 10 Thu - Week 11 Thu This assessment will take place during the scheduled tutorial times for this course (Week 10 and Week 11)
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Peer assessment factor, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: The Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games present both opportunities and challenges for tourism and events organisations. In this assessment, your group will apply scenario planning techniques to explore a plausible future Brisbane tourism environment in 2032 and develop strategic recommendations that will enable Brisbane to thrive under that future scenario. Following the presentation, each student will participate in an individual Q&A. Group Presentation: Present the analysis and recommendations in class, with feedback provided by classmates in hypothetical roles as the senior management of the tourism or event organisation. Maximum 15 minutes per group. Peer Assessment Factor for this assessment: Conducted online, at the conclusion of all presentations (% fulfilment of individual role x actual mark awarded to group) Individual Q&A: Following the presentation, each student will participate in an individual Q&A (Maximum 3-5 minutes per student). Students are expected to demonstrate individual understanding of the entire presentation. Please Note: The presentation and Q&A will be recorded for marking purposes. Stakeholder Mapping (A1 Activity 3) Students map stakeholders involved in Brisbane 2032 tourism planning and identify competing interests. Tutorial discussion on sustainability conflicts and governance challenges Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
